canada.title: $200K from N.L. going to downtown St. John’s for private security foot patrols
canada.summary: On Thursday Newfoundland and Labrador’s justice minister announced $200,000 in funding to boost safety in downtown St. John’s, which is going towards uniformed foot patrols. Downtown St. John’s chair Jonathan Loder says it will act as a deterrent against crime.

canada.title: 1 person injured in stabbing near Toronto’s Kensington Market
canada.summary: One person is in hospital following a stabbing near Toronto’s Kensington Market on Sunday morning.

canada.title: Historic N.S. lighthouse receives grants for repairs
canada.summary: Sandy Point Lighthouse, a 150-year-old landmark on Nova Scotia's southwestern shore, has secured federal and municipal grants to keep it from collapsing into the sea.

canada.title: Tumbler Ridge begins consultation on design for new school building
canada.summary: Six people were killed in Tumbler Ridge when 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar opened fire at the northeastern B.C. school on Feb. 10.

canada.title: Blackhawks’ Kaiser suspended three games
canada.summary: Chicago Blackhawks defenceman Wyatt Kaiser has been suspended for three games for an illegal check to the head of Calgary Flames forward Martin Pospisil, the NHL's Department of Player Safety announced on Sunday.

canada.title: Pay halted for suspended Vancouver police officer charged with fraud and theft
canada.summary: The Vancouver Police Board has discontinued pay for a high-profile officer accused of fraud and theft.

canada.title: N.B. cadet volunteers, parents push back as military halts flights, competitions
canada.summary: New Brunswick cadet volunteers and parents say a national funding pause has cancelled gliding and competitions, scaled back marksmanship and reduced paid training time for officers until at least March. National Defence says the program's budget grew to $265 million this year to meet rising enrolment and that weekly training nights will continue.

canada.title: Housing project in Brossard, Que., promised affordability. Residents said no
canada.summary: The City of Brossard is asking a developer to go back to the drawing board after a group of residents blocked a housing project that would have brought 810 units, including affordable housing, to the city's edge.

canada.title: Community groups blindsided as Ottawa pauses refugee sponsorship program
canada.summary: The federal government has quietly pressed pause on a program that helped community groups sponsor and support refugees come to Canada.

canada.title: 2 teens dead, 1 injured after shooting at Scarborough gas station: Toronto police
canada.summary: Toronto police are investigating a homicide after two 16-year-old boys died and another sustained serious injuries following a shooting in Scarborough in the early hours of Sunday.

canada.title: First residents to move into new Saint John modular home community in December
canada.summary: Three levels of government announced $17.2 million Friday for United Way Maritimes' Sunnyside community in Saint John, N.B. The 70 modular homes will house people experiencing chronic homelessness, with 24-hour support on site. The first residents are expected to move in mid-December.

canada.title: 2 pedestrians hospitalized after separate collisions in Winnipeg
canada.summary: Two pedestrians were hospitalized after two separate vehicle collisions in Winnipeg over the weekend, police say.

canada.title: Quebec students consider general strike to protest affordability crisis
canada.summary: Post-secondary students in Montreal gathered on Saturday to vote on an indefinite strike to protest a perceived lack of funding for higher education in Quebec.

canada.title: 'We cannot delay': N.L. scientist observing climate change on 8-month Arctic expedition
canada.summary: Marine Institute Scientist Maxime Geoffroy has a new home for the next five months, and it’s atop a sheet of ice in the Arctic Ocean. He's on a research marathon with a team of 12 that has already seen the effects of climate change before their very eyes.

canada.title: Manitoba government quietly ends court fine work program, then reinstates it after concerns raised
canada.summary: The Manitoba government has reinstated a program that allows people to work off court fines they couldn't otherwise afford to pay, after quietly phasing it out last month.

canada.title: How firearms regulations are changing the RCMP Heritage Centre
canada.summary: The RCMP Heritage Centre in Regina, which is set to become Canada's next national museum, has taken out all firearms on display in cases, to comply with provincial firearms regulations. Replica guns should be on display in the new year.

canada.title: Proposed gondola overlooking Canmore seeks public feedback
canada.summary: A gondola project that has been a contentious topic in Canmore for almost a decade is likely to get a decision in early 2027.

canada.title: Badly needed construction materials could be rotting outside for years, Nunavut leaders say
canada.summary: Nunavut leaders say building materials for desperately needed homes in their communities are being left unattended for years. Those materials can end up unusable, delaying construction even more
